Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business

rate noun

so much a day or a month: pay, interest, exchange

also hourly rate, daily rate, rate of pay, interest rate, exchange rate, per day

classical

Tac. Ann. 1.17: dēnīs in diem assibus (Lewis & Short)

in diem

phrase: in with the accusative

a day, per day

Latin has no noun for a rate: it puts the price in the ablative and the unit after in, dēnīs in diem assibus, at ten asses a day; for every year, in singulōs annōs (Cic. Att. 6.3.5).

Other words

  • mercēs, mercēdis f. — pay, wages, a fee

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Sall. Cat. 37.7: manuum mercēde inopiam tolerāre (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

  • centēsimae, centēsimārum f. pl. — interest at one per cent a month, twelve a year

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 6.3.5 · Declension on Wiktionary

    The standard Roman rate of interest; a third of it was triēns, two thirds bēs (Cic. Att. 4.15.7). See interest, on money lent.

  • collybus, collybī m. — the rate of exchange; the money-changer’s premium

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.3.181 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 12.6.1 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Greek κόλλυβος.

Examples

  • dēnīs in diem assibus animam et corpus aestimārī

    (they complain) that body and soul are valued at ten asses a dayTac. Ann. 1.17

  • Scaptius centēsimīs, renovātō in singulōs annōs faenore, contentus nōn fuit

    Scaptius was not content with twelve per cent, with the interest added to the debt every yearCic. Att. 6.3.5

See also price, percent, interest, change money.
